ap_statistics-m01.set_intro: Questions refer to the following information. In a certain process, a clinic phones a random sample of $5$ patients from a large list on which $40\%$ of the patients missed their last appointment. Let $X$ be the number of patients in the sample who missed an appointment. The probability distribution of $X$ is shown in the table.

stimulus.description: Probability distribution of X, the number of patients in the sample who missed an appointment

items.stem: What is the mean (expected value) of $X$? Round to two decimal places.

options.why: Uses $n/2$, as if each outcome had probability $0.5$.
The mean of a binomial random variable is $np = 5(0.4) = 2$; weighting each value of $X$ by its probability in the table gives the same value.
Reports the probability of one outcome instead of the mean of $X$.
Uses $n(1-p)$, the expected number of non-defective outcomes, instead of $np$.

blueprint.subject: ap_statistics
blueprint.concept: Find the mean of a random variable from its probability distribution
student_thinking: Recognize that the mean of X weights each value by its probability, or equals np for a binomial random variable
Distinguish the mean from the most likely value and from the expected number of the other outcome

key_conditions.condition: the mean of a binomial random variable is n times p
key_conditions.evidence: the table gives the distribution and the stem gives n and the percent of defective outcomes

misconceptions.description: reports p instead of the mean
reports the most likely value as the mean

verification.independent_path: the mean is recomputed as the sum of x times P(X = x) over the table and compared with n times p

items.stem: What is the probability that at least $2$ of the patients in the sample missed an appointment? Use the table and round to three decimal places.

options.why: Subtracts only $P(X=1)$ from $1$, leaving out the probability that $X=0$ from the removed values.
Finds $P(X > 2)$, leaving out the probability that $X = 2$.
$P(X \ge 2) = 1 - P(X=0) - P(X=1) = 1 - 0.0778 - 0.2592 \approx 0.663$, which equals the sum of the table probabilities from $x=2$ on.
Finds $P(X = 2)$ only, instead of the probability of $2$ or more.

blueprint.subject: ap_statistics
blueprint.concept: Find an at-least probability from a probability distribution table
student_thinking: Translate at least 2 into the values 2 and above of X
Add those probabilities or subtract the probabilities of the values below 2 from 1

key_conditions.condition: P(X at least 2) equals one minus the probabilities of 0 and 1
key_conditions.evidence: the table lists the probability of every value of X

misconceptions.description: uses more than 2 instead of at least 2
uses exactly 2 instead of at least 2

verification.independent_path: the table probabilities are summed from x = 2 up and compared with the complement, using binomial probabilities computed from the combinations formula and scipy

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of $P(X=0)$ in this context?

options.text: In about $8\%$ of all such random samples of $5$ patients, none of the patients would have missed an appointment
options.why: $P(X=0) \approx 0.0778$ is the long-run proportion of random samples of $5$ patients in which none of the patients missed an appointment.

options.text: There is a $8\%$ chance that any one of the patients in a sample missed an appointment
options.why: Confuses $P(X=0)$ with the probability for one individual item; the probability for one patient is given in the scenario.

options.text: Exactly $8\%$ of the patients in every sample of $5$ missed an appointment
options.why: Reads a probability as a guaranteed percentage in every sample.

options.text: In about $8\%$ of all such samples, all of the patients would have missed an appointment
options.why: Reverses the event: $X=0$ means none are of the stated kind, not all.

blueprint.subject: ap_statistics
blueprint.concept: Interpret a probability from a distribution in context
student_thinking: Read P(X = 0) from the table and recall what the event X = 0 means in words
Interpret a probability as a long-run proportion of repeated random samples

key_conditions.condition: a probability from a distribution describes the long-run proportion of samples with that outcome
key_conditions.evidence: the table gives P(X = 0) and the scenario defines X

misconceptions.description: confuses with the probability for one item
reads it as a guaranteed percentage

verification.independent_path: the sentences are generated from the definition of X and the table value; the event wording is checked against X = 0

ap_statistics-m02.set_intro: Questions refer to the following information. The relationship between the age of a used car, in years, and its selling price, in thousands of dollars, is described by a least-squares regression line. Computer output for the regression is shown.

stimulus.description: Computer output for a least-squares regression

items.stem: Which of the following is the correct interpretation of the slope of the regression line?

options.text: For each additional year of age, the selling price decreases by exactly $1.76$ thousand dollars
options.why: Claims an exact change for every individual, but the slope describes the predicted change on average.

options.text: For each additional year of age, the predicted selling price decreases by about $1.76$ thousand dollars
options.why: The slope is $-1.76$, so each one-year increase in age goes with a predicted change of $-1.76$ thousand dollars in selling price.

options.text: For each additional $1.76$ thousand dollars of selling price, the predicted age decreases by about $1$ year
options.why: Reverses the roles of the explanatory and the response variables.

options.text: For each additional year of age, the predicted selling price decreases by about $1.76\%$
options.why: Treats the slope as a percent change instead of a change in the units of the response.

blueprint.subject: ap_statistics
blueprint.concept: Interpret the slope of a least-squares line in context
student_thinking: Read the slope from the Coef column next to the explanatory variable
Describe the predicted change in the response for a one-unit increase in the explanatory variable, in context and with units

key_conditions.condition: the slope is the predicted change in y for a one-unit increase in x
key_conditions.evidence: the output gives the slope in the Coef column and the stem names both variables and their units

verification.independent_path: the interpretation sentences are generated from the slope sign and units, and the slope is checked against the sign implied by the correlation

items.stem: What is the predicted selling price when age is $7$? Round to one decimal place.

options.why: The predicted value is $\hat y = 24.3 + (-1.76)(7) \approx 12.0$.
Leaves out the intercept and predicts with the slope times $x$ alone.
Adds the slope to the intercept instead of multiplying the slope by $x$.
Uses the slope as the intercept and the intercept as the slope.

blueprint.subject: ap_statistics
blueprint.concept: Predict a response value from regression output
student_thinking: Read the intercept and the slope from the Coef column
Substitute the x value into the line and round as stated

key_conditions.condition: the predicted value is intercept plus slope times x
key_conditions.evidence: the output gives both coefficients and the stem gives x

verification.independent_path: the prediction is recomputed from the printed coefficients and compared with the generating line

items.stem: What is the correlation coefficient between the two variables? Round to two decimal places.

options.why: Divides $r$ by $2$, which has no basis in the output.
Reports $r^2$ as if it were the correlation $r$.
The correlation has the same sign as the slope, so $r = -\sqrt{0.81} = -0.90$.
Uses the wrong sign: the sign of $r$ must match the sign of the slope.

blueprint.subject: ap_statistics
blueprint.concept: Find the correlation coefficient from R-squared and the sign of the slope
student_thinking: Take the square root of the R-Sq value written as a proportion
Give r the same sign as the slope

key_conditions.condition: r is the square root of r squared with the sign of the slope
key_conditions.evidence: the output shows R-Sq and the slope

verification.independent_path: r is recomputed as the square root of the printed R-Sq with the slope's sign and rounded to two decimals; options are at least 0.04 apart
